correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact JR definition, violating groups are in one-to-one existential correspondence with excluded candidates receiving at least r=ceil(n/k) approvals among voters with no elected approval. Those voters form Bin(n,q_W); conditional outside candidate counts are independent Bin(u,p_c), proving equation (1). Monotone binomial coupling gives monotonicity in q and excluded p, so each exchange replacing an elected low-p candidate by an excluded high-p candidate increases J. For top-k, all failure witness counts have Bin(n,a_c) laws with a_c<=p_c(1-p_c)^k<=a_k<1/k, giving Chernoff and the union bound. The equal-probability vector p*=1/(k+1) supplies a matching single-candidate binomial lower tail; standard Stirling asymptotics (or exact p^n for k=1) prove the limiting equality. Endpoint probabilities, m=k, integer rounding, and finite-input arithmetic complexity are treated explicitly. Independent exhaustive small-instance rational enumeration passed 81 direct assertions but is not relied on as an infinite proof.

The new claim only concerns the additional exact finite-n and sharp universal quantitative information.

originality.rationale: The central exact finite-electorate JR mixture, its distribution-wise finite-n probability-maximizing top-k committee, and a parameter-uniform sharp large-deviation failure exponent were compared by statement and logical implication with the closely related 2024 uncertainty-hardness paper, the 2021/22 common-probability JR threshold paper, the 2025 stronger CORE/EJR+ asymptotic result, and empirical 2019 literature. The qualitative asymptotic guarantee and the maximum of p(1-p)^k are known and excluded from novelty. The inspected results did not state or logically determine the full finite-n/optimality/sharp-exponent conjunction. This is a self-review with residual priority risk, not a global uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: The binomial-mixture identity or finite-n top-k optimizer might have appeared in uninspected supplemental or later independent work despite the targeted searches.
The sharp universal rate refines a known common-p binomial argument and may follow from an existing broader probabilistic result not explicitly compared.
Only self-review has been performed; independent publication-priority assessment is not yet available.

value.rationale: General uncertain-voter JR counting and MaxJR are hard, whereas candidate-specific probability estimates shared across voters define a natural and strictly non-deterministic restricted class. A closed form evaluating arbitrary n,m,k without enumerating approval profiles, a globally optimal committee for every finite n, and a best-possible distribution-uniform failure rate address statistical reliability and algorithmic committee design. These are more than a textbook binomial inequality in isolation: the exact mixture and exchange principle eliminate general-parameter computational hardness in a motivated model, and the sharp global exponent adds a meaningful quantitative guarantee. Previously established qualitative high-probability JR and a_k maximization are not counted as new.
